The facts leading to pass the present award are that Police has filed a Detailed Accident Report (DAR) with respect to accident occurred on 05.04.2017 within the jurisdiction of P.S Uttam Nagar, Delhi.

Brief facts of the present case are that on 05.04.2017, at about 02.25 p.m, the petitioner was waiting for school bus for receiving her son on the footpath near Metro Piller No.771 at Najafgarh, Uttam Nagar Road, Delhi within the jurisdiction of P.S Uttam Nagar, Delhi.

When a ERickshaw No. DL9ER 1146 being driven by respondent No.1 in rash and negligent manner,
hit the petitioner and run over the leg of petitioner.
As a result of which petitioner received grievous injuries in her leg.
The petitioner suffered grievous injury on her leg.
She was removed to Dr Badhwar Nurshing Home Main Najafgarh Uttam ,Delhi for her treatment where she remained admitted in hospital for two days.

sentences.text: 9. PW 1 has duly been cross examined on behalf of respondent No.3, insurance company.
The testimony of the PW1 with respect to negligent driving by R.1 could not be impeached.
Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
The evidence which has come on the file can be considered and becomes more relevant when there is no specific evidence led by other side in rebuttal.
Even otherwise strict rule that negligence is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt is not to be proved in MACT proceedings.
The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof.
Therefore, the evidence which has come on the file only can be considered.
The charge sheet was filed against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against such implication.
He was not possessing any D/L at the time of accident.

So this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondents by holding that petitioner suffered injuries in a vehicular accident due to rash and negligent driving of offending ( E Rickshaw No. DL9ER1146) bearing No. DL 9S AR0329 by respondent No.1 ISSUE No.2: ?
Whether the petitioners in the above mentioned is entitled to compensation , if so , what amount and from whom?...

sentences.text: Ld Counsel for the insurance company has submitted that there is no loss of income of the petitioner as petitioner is a housewife.
Ld. counsel for petitioners submitted that even if the victim/injured was housewife, she cannot be treated having no income of her own.

This Tribunal while relying upon a case titled as Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Master Manmeet Singh & Ors MAC.APP.
590/2011 decided by our own Hon'be High Court on 30.01.2012.

sentences.text: It is observed by the Hon'b le High Court that value of services rendered by such home maker should be taken as minimum wages of a nonmatriculate (in the absence of any evidence to the contrary).
So this Tribunal while assessing the income of injured under Minimum Wages Act prevailing in Delhi has assessed the income of injured under the head of Non matriculate as Rs.14,958/ p.m.
The petitioner has suffered grievous in her left leg and multiple abrasions .

Seeing the nature of injuries on the person of petitioner, which may took considerable time to heal up, so an amount of Rs.59,832/ ( ie four months MACT No. 1002/17 Poonam Gupta Vs. Rambir &
Ors. Page No. 9 of 13 Minimum wages of nonmatric ) is awarded to the petitioner for loss of earning.

Pain and Suffering:
13.

The next point that is to be discussed is pain and suffering and to calculate the same, the nature of injuries caused to the injured due to the accident, duration for which he got medical treatment and she was constrained to live in bed are few factors which must be taken into account.
It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his/her complete life, the mental agony which he or she faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
To compensate petitioner under this head, a sum of Rs.50,000/ is awarded to him.

Mental and physical shock:
14.
Petitioner was of 35 years of age at the time of accident.

But due to this mishappening with her,
her expectations got completely shattered which cannot be compensated in monetary terms.
However, to console her to an extent, a sum of Rs25,000/ is awarded to petitioner under this head.

Conveyance and Special Diet:
15.
The next point to be discussed is conveyance & special diet, though, petitioner has not produced any evidence with regard to conveyance charges.
But considering the fact that petitioner remained under treatment for a considerable time.
She is granted Rs. 10,000/ towards conveyance and Rs.10,000/ towards special diet.

opennyai_summary.facts:
When a ERickshaw No. DL9ER 1146 being driven by respondent No.1 in rash and negligent manner,
hit the petitioner and run over the leg of petitioner.
As a result of which petitioner received grievous injuries in her leg.
The petitioner suffered grievous injury on her leg.
She was removed to Dr Badhwar Nurshing Home Main Najafgarh Uttam ,Delhi for her treatment where she remained admitted in hospital for two days.
After completion of investigation, investigating agency contended that said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing E Rickshaw No. DL9ER1146 being driven by Rambir (driver), who has been made respondent no. 1.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner is entitled to claim compensation , if so , what amount and from whom?
So this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondents by holding that petitioner suffered injuries in a vehicular accident due to rash and negligent driving of offending ( E Rickshaw No. DL9ER1146) bearing No. DL 9S AR0329 by respondent No.1 ISSUE No.2: ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
9. PW 1 has duly been cross examined on behalf of respondent No.3, insurance company.
The testimony of the PW1 with respect to negligent driving by R.1 could not be impeached.
Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing of a claim under MACT, is not that strict as it is under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
The evidence which has come on the file can be considered and becomes more relevant when there is no specific evidence led by other side in rebuttal.
Even otherwise strict rule that negligence is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt is not to be proved in MACT proceedings.
The allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof.
Therefore, the evidence which has come on the file only can be considered.
The charge sheet was filed against respondent no.1 and he has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against such implication.
He was not possessing any D/L at the time of accident.
It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his/her complete life, the mental agony which he or she faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
To compensate petitioner under this head, a sum of Rs.50,000/ is awarded to him.

The Bank Manager, as mentioned in column no.24 of FormV of the petitioner's bank, is directed to convert the 80% of the award amount alongwith interest in two FDR commencing from one year to two year in the said MACT BANK ACCOUNT of petitioner and after receiving the amount credited in his MACAD ACCOUNT ( Motor Accident Claim Annuity deposit )
MACT No. 1002/17 Poonam Gupta Vs. Rambir & Ors. Page No. 12 of 13 22.

(ii) The interest on the fixed deposit be paid monthly.
(iii) The monthly interest be credited automatically in the saving account of the claimant.
(iv) Original fixed deposit receipt be retained by the bank in safe custody.
